insights.claim: The gateway has no authentication enforcement of its own; it relies entirely on the upstream infrastructure or orchestrator to validate Authorization headers it forwards.
insights.reasoning: The gateway forwards Authorization headers to the orchestrator but does not validate, decode, or reject requests lacking credentials. If deployed without an upstream authentication proxy (e.g., Istio, OAuth proxy), the gateway accepts unauthenticated requests. This is a deployment-topology-dependent security posture.

insights.claim: The gateway's inbound listener uses plain HTTP without TLS, while outbound connections to the orchestrator support optional mTLS.
insights.reasoning: The axum server binds a plain TCP listener (no TLS) on port 8090, while the reqwest client to the orchestrator optionally establishes mTLS when certificates are mounted. This asymmetry means the gateway-to-orchestrator leg can be encrypted, but client-to-gateway traffic is unencrypted unless an upstream proxy or service mesh provides TLS termination.

insights.claim: FIPS compliance is delegated to the system OpenSSL provider on UBI 9; the application does not explicitly select or verify FIPS mode.
insights.reasoning: The Rust binary uses the openssl and native-tls crates which delegate to the system OpenSSL library. On RHEL 9/UBI 9 in FIPS mode, OpenSSL 3.0 uses the FIPS provider automatically. However, the application code does not assert FIPS mode, select cipher suites, or verify the active provider. FIPS compliance is entirely implicit and depends on the host configuration.
